brief: Goldman's Privorotsky argued hedge funds' 11-point tech underweight, short dealer gamma, and holiday seasonality could squeeze the S&P higher if it stabilized into Thanksgiving; he noted dealer gamma cuts both ways. Instead, after briefly rallying on Anthropic's IPO pricing, the S&P fell back below its 200-day moving average by 10:45am, closing down as much as 1.5% for a sixth straight decline, the longest since April 2024, with all 11 sectors red. BTIG's Krinsky found only three 30-year precedents for six-day losing streaks closing below the 200DMA by less than 3%: 2000, 2018, and 2020. Each saw a bounce (avg 3.9%) within five days, followed by a much larger drawdown (avg 24%), though Krinsky's own target stays 7,000-7,100, not extrapolating that drawdown. He argues more downside is coming because the market hasn't capitulated (74% downside volume, Apple down under 1%). Krinsky also turned bearish on healthcare (XLV, target 175) as defensives cracked, while easing (not reversing) his bearish gold call near his $3,500 target. Zero Hedge sides with Krinsky over Privorotsky for what comes next.
